dyuot: dyuot (dyfod) — to come; verbal noun (a dyuot y Lynn Cuch 'and coming to Glyn Cuch')
y: y — (1) the article 'the' (y llys); (2) 'his, her, its' (y uryt: soft mutation = his; y hymdidan: h-prefix = her); (3) 'to' (y hela, y gyuoeth); (4) preverbal particle after a fronted adverb or object (yno y bu, Pwyll... a oed); (5) the relative in oblique relations (o'r a welsei) · (6) 'from' in y gan, y wrth 'from, compared with' (y gan y uarch 'from his horse'; y wrth y ffryt hi 'compared with her form'); (7) infixed object 'him, her, it' after a (a'y guelei 'who saw her'); (8) in a'y kymriw it is the second letter of ae 'either' (see a) · also (9) y am, y amdanaw 'from about, off' (y amdanaw 'off him'); y am hynny 'around that, beyond that, besides' · also (10) 'their' (for eu), with no mutation (y bot 'their being'; y kymryt 'their taking' = to take them) · also (11) 'in' (y'th wlat ti 'in your country') · (12) the particle y before mae introducing a reported fact (y may brawt … a wnaeth hynny 'that it is a brother who did that') · also (13) for predicative yn 'as', with soft mutation (Mi a rodaf Duw y uach it 'I give God as surety to you'; the Red Book yn vach)
r: 'r — the article yr contracted after a vowel, apostrophe half of a'r, y'r, o'r etc.: 'the'
ystauell: ystauell (ystafell) — room, chamber; noun f. (na guas ystauell 'no chamber-servant')
yn: yn — (1) 'in' (yn Arberth; nasal mutation: yn nyblyc); (2) predicative 'as' with soft mutation (yn wisc hela, yn arglwyd); (3) with a verbal noun, progressive (yn dyuot 'coming'); (4) before an adjective, adverbial (yn llawen 'gladly') · (5) yn yd 'to where' (ymchwelut yn yd oed Pwyll 'returning to where Pwyll was') · also yn yd 'as, while, when' (Ac yn yd aeth pawb ym pen yr arueu 'and while all went to arms'; the sense uncertain) · also 'our', a spelling of an (ein), with no mutation (yn anniuer ninheu 'our own company'; yn ymborth 'our sustenance'; yn diuetha 'our destroying')
yd: yd — preverbal particle used when the clause opens with an adverb rather than the subject, introducing an indicative main verb (A threigylgweith yd oed yn Arberth)
oed: bot (bod) — to be; 3 sg. imperfect 'was' (Pwyll... a oed yn arglwyd) · also oed 'appointed time, tryst', noun m., = oet (gwna oed a mi 'make an appointment with me')
kicua: Kicua (Cigfa) — proper name, the wife Pryderi chose, daughter of Gwyn Gohoyw; no mutation
a: a — (1) preverbal/relative particle before a verb, causes soft mutation (Pwyll … a oed; ef a welei); (2) 'and' before a consonant, spirant mutation (a chanu, a fob); (3) 'with' (a'y gydymdeithon; gyt a thi); (4) vocative particle (A unben); (5) 'whoever, what' before a verb (a del 'whoever may come'; a wnaethost 'what you did') · (6) 3 sg. present of mynet 'goes' (nat a odyno 'that he does not go from there'; yd a hitheu 'she goes'); (7) interrogative particle before a verb (a oes …? 'is there …?'; a dywedy di …? 'will you tell …?'); (8) in a'y kymriw neu archolleu the editorial a'y stands for the conjunction ae 'either' (ae … neu 'either … or'; the Red Book has ae kymriw ae archolleu): read the two halves together as ae · (9) 'as' after an equative (kyn debycket a'r mab 'as like as the boy'; kyn ureisket oed a mab chweblwyd 'as stout as a boy of six') · also 'to, towards' with spirant mutation (parth a Hardlech 'towards Harlech'; y tu a Chernyw 'the side towards Cornwall') · also (10) linking a fronted adjective to its noun, with soft mutation of the noun (ys drwc a gedymdeith 'a bad companion'); here a is not the conjunction
goleuhau: goleuhau (goleuo; GPC goleuhau) — to grow light, brighten, light up; verbal noun after yn (llyma yn goleuhau pob lle 'behold, every place growing light'); no mutation
tan: tan (tân) — fire; noun m. (y tan a'r glo 'the fire and the charcoal'); no mutation
ac: a — 'and' before a vowel (ac ef); also the preposition a 'with' before a vowel (ymgael ac ef 'meet with him', ymordiwes ac ef) · the manuscript also writes ac before some consonants (Ac wal, Ac val, ac racdaw) · also 'as' after an equative or kymeint (kymeint ac ynot ti 'as much as in you'; mor anwedus ac ar y wnaethoed 'as unseemly as what she had done')
wrth: wrth (wrth) — to, towards, according to; preposition, base form (dywedut... wrthaw) · also 'at' (wrth y danned 'at the teeth'; wrth yr ascwrn 'at the bone') and 'because of' (wrth hynny 'for that reason')
dodi: dodi (dodi) — to put; verbal noun (dodi y deudroet yn y got 'to put his two feet in the bag'; dodi llef ar y gorn 'to give a blast on the horn')
uanec: maneg (maneg) — glove; noun f. (spelt manec); soft-mutated (m>u, = f) after y, whether the feminine article or 'his' (yn y uanec 'in his glove')
ar: ar — (1) preposition 'on, upon; at' (ar Hafgan; ar y carw; ar y gilyd 'against the other'); (2) the article yr after a vowel, 'that which' (noc ar a uu 'than what was'; Ar ny del 'and whoever does not come') · also (3) 'with, accompanied by' (ar y ganuet marchauc 'with his hundred horsemen'); 'in' (ar y ssynnwyr e hun 'in his own senses'; ar perued y digrifwch 'in the middle of the merriment'); ar neill law Pwyll 'on one side of Pwyll'; ar uyrr 'quickly'; ar hynny 'thereupon' (see yny) · also 'over' (ar yr ynys hon 'over this island'); 'after the manner of' (ar ureint kyweirdeb 'in the manner of the arrangement'); 'on' a decision (disgynnu ar gymryt hynny 'settled on taking that'); 'ar ol' 'after' (ar ol Matholwch 'after Matholwch'); ar dec 'on ten' (see dec) · also 'concerning, about', where am would be expected (ac ar Yspydaut Benn 'and concerning the Hospitality of the Head'; the Red Book also ar)
oruc: gwneuthur (gwneud) — to do, make; 3 sg. preterite auxiliary 'he did', soft-mutated after a, with g dropped (kyuodi a oruc)
beth: beth — what; interrogative pronoun (beth amgen 'what else?', beth a wnaf 'what shall I do?')
yssyd: bot (bod) — to be; relative present 'is, who/that is' (sydd) (Gwr yssyd gyuerbyn; pa amgen uedwl yssyd yndaw)
yna: yna (yna) — then; adverb (Yna y rodes Arawn y furuf)
arglwyd: arglwyd (arglwydd) — lord; noun m., term of address
heb: heb — (1) 'said' (heb ef 'said he'), a defective verb used only for tagging speech; (2) 'without' + verbal noun (heb hanbwyllaw 'without troubling') · (3) 'past, beside' in heb law (heb law yr orssed 'past the mound'); see hebdaw · also 'without' + noun (heb ohir 'without delay')
ynteu: ynteu (yntau) — 'he, for his part'; conjunctive pronoun marking a change of speaker or actor (heb ynteu)
geueis: caffael (cael) — to get; 1 sg. preterite 'I got' (a geueis i yn gedymdeith 'that I got as a companion')
arnaf: ar — conjugated preposition 'on me' (arnaf i 'on me')
pa: pa (pa) — what, which; interrogative adjective, triggers soft mutation of the following noun
ryw: ryw (rhyw) — some, some kind of; before its noun (ryw ystyr hut 'some meaning of magic') · also y ryw wr 'what kind of man'; ryw 'sort, kind' as a noun
th: 'th — infixed/proclitic pronoun, apostrophe half of a'th, i'th, dy'th etc.: 'your' (possessive) or 'you' (object)
hi: hi — 'she, her'; independent 3 sg. f. pronoun
llyma: llyma (dyma) — behold, here is; presentative particle throwing a scene before the reader (llyma yr erchwys)
oll: oll (oll) — all, wholly; adverb/adjective intensifying a preceding noun (yr arueu oll 'all the armour')
menegi: menegi (mynegi) — to tell, relate; verbal noun (menegi y holl gyfranc a wnaeth idi)
ual: ual (fel) — as, like; conjunction/preposition (ual hynn 'like this') · also 'so that' (ual yd ymglywynt 'so that they could hear one another'; ual y bydynt gadarnach 'so that they would be stronger') and 'how' (sef ual yd eistedyssant 'that is how they sat')
yr: yr — (1) the article 'the' before a vowel (yr erchwys); (2) 'for, for the sake of' preposition (yr Duw 'for God's sake', yr guaret gormes 'for removing the oppression') · (3) 'for all, however' before an equative-type noun and a clause (yr araued y kerdei y uarch 'for all the slowness with which his horse went'); (4) in yr meityn 'for a while (since)'; (5) the verbal particle y, yd, written yr before a vowel (yr ymordiwedei a hi 'that he would overtake her') · also (6) the perfective particle ry written yr, softening the verb (yr gyscwys 'has slept'); the article before an independent possessive (yr eidunt 'theirs'); 'for' with an abstract noun (yr bychanet 'for the smallness') · also the article before hwnn, honn, 'the one' (yr hwnn y tu a Chernyw 'the one on the side towards Cornwall'; yr honn a uu tryded anuat paluawt 'the one that was the third unfortunate blow') · also yr (er) 'for all' before the relative a (yr a welsynt o ouut 'for all the grief they had seen') · also the article before a consonant in kyrchu yr gaer 'making for the fort' (read as the article, as the second witness takes it)
idaw: idaw (iddo) — to him; 3 sg. m. conjugated form of y 'to'
doethant: dyuot (dod) — to come; 3 pl. preterite 'they came' (Y'r llys y doethant 'to the court they came')
llygot: llygot (llygod) — mice; plural of llygoden; noun (y llygot 'the mice'); radical after the article
grofd: kroft (croft) — croft, small field (from English croft); noun f., written grofd with d. In this part the word is always grofd, even where nothing softens: after teir (a'e deir grofd), which does not soften the next word, and as the object of a verbal noun (edrych grofd arall 'to look at another croft'), as well as after the feminine article and the feminine ordinal (y grofd, y tryded grofd), where softening would be regular. The scribe seems to take grofd as the word's own form (compare o'e rofdeu, and the Red Book y rofft, y dryded rofft)
wyd: gwyd (cf. gwedd) — manner, way; noun, soft-mutated after llyma (Llyma wyd y kyffy 'here is the way you will get it') · also 'presence, keeping' (gwydd), soft after dy 'your' (y'th wyd di 'to your presence, into your keeping')
un: un (un) — one; numeral/adjective (un dyrnaut 'one blow') · also 'same' (yn un ansawd 'in the same appearance'; yr un ford 'the same way') and the pronoun 'one (of them)' (Un a gyuodes 'one rose')
ohonunt: o (o) + wynt — 'of them, from them'; conjugated preposition, 3 pl. (kyscu a wnaeth pawb ohonunt 'every one of them slept'); no mutation
amdrom: amdrom (no modern form) — very heavy; adjective, am- + trom (the feminine of trwm 'heavy', for the mouse), trom softened (t>d) after am- inside the compound; yn amdrom 'heavy', predicative; perhaps heavy with young (uncertain)
inheu: inheu (innau) — I/mine, for my part; conjunctive 1 sg. pronoun marking contrast (a'm kyuoeth inheu 'my realm, mine')
auory: auory (yfory) — tomorrow; adverb (o'r dyd auory 'from the day tomorrow')
ym: yn (yn) — in; preposition, spelling variant before p/m/b (hyt ym Penn Llwyn Diarwya; ym perued) · also bot 1 pl. present 'we are' (yd ym y gyt 'we are together'; llibin yd ym pob blwydyn 'wretched that we are every year') · also 'my', a by-form of uy, in the oath ym kyffes y Duw 'by my confession to God' (the Red Book has ym kyffes i y Duw); the nasal mutation it brings is not written
kyffes: kyffes (cyffes) — confession; noun f. (ym kyffes y Duw 'by my confession to God'; the Red Book has ym kyffes i y Duw); ym is taken as 'my', and the nasal mutation it brings (nghyffes) is not shown in the spelling
bei: bot (bod) — to be; 3 sg. imperfect subjunctive 'were, would be' (bei ar y gam 'if it were at its step' = at a walk) · also the conjunction 'if' (bei ymladem ni ac wyntwy 'if we fought with them')
caffwn: caffael (cael) — to get; 1 sg. imperfect subjunctive 'I were to get' (pei caffwn dewis 'if I could have my choice')
mi: mi — 1 sg. independent/emphatic pronoun 'I' (mi a wnn 'I know')
diryued: diryued (di- + rhyfedd) — no wonder; predicate (Diryued oed hynny 'that was no wonder')
hynny: hynny — 'that (thing)'; demonstrative pronoun, very frequent (a hynny 'and that')
eisswys: eissoes (eisoes) — yet, nevertheless, already; adverb, spelt eisswys (ac yn hynny eisswys, kyn hanner noss 'and in that, nevertheless, before midnight'); no mutation
yw: bot (bod) — to be; present 3 sg. copula 'is', used in equative sentences (Sef yw hwnnw, Hafgan)
guelet: gwelet (gweld) — to see; verbal noun, gu for gw (A guelet a wnaeth 'and he saw')
gwr: gwr (gŵr) — man; noun m. (y gwr a oed yn lle Arawn 'the man who was in Arawn's place')
kyuurd: kyuurd (cyfurdd) — of equal rank, of the same degree; adjective, kyf- 'co-' + urdd 'rank' (morwyn gystal, kyuurd 'a maiden so good, of equal rank'); no mutation
hwnnw: hwnnw (hwnnw) — 'that' (m.); demonstrative (y dyd hwnnw 'that day') · also pronoun 'that one' (A hwnnw uu y trydyd dyn 'and that one was the third man'; yw hwnnw 'that is it')
phei: pei (pe) — if; spirant-mutated after a 'and' (a phei); in a phei … pellaf … 'and the more … the farther' it works like modern po
iawn: iawn — right, proper, correct; adjective/predicate (iawn yw gymryt 'it is right to receive') · also noun 'compensation, redress, amends' (dy iawn 'your compensation'; chael iawn 'getting redress')
nyt: ny (nid) — negative particle 'not, it is not', spelling before a vowel or in emphasis (nyt teilygdawt)
namyn: namyn (namyn) — except, but; conjunction (namyn ti 'but you')
ellwng: gollwng (gollwng) — to loose, release; verbal noun (ellwng e gwn 'to loose his hounds')
e: y — 'his', spelt e before a following consonant or in some spellings: e gwn 'his dogs', e weneb 'his face'; also the preposition 'to' in e uynet 'to go' · also 'her', with h- before a vowel (e hymlit hi 'to pursue her'); the verbal particle y (e deuthum i 'I came'); y of y wrth 'from' (e wrthaw 'from him'); and in e uynyd 'up', e ymdeith 'away' · also the article 'the' (E brenhin, E chwedyl 'the king', 'the news'); 'it' as dummy subject (E doeth im 'it came to me') · also the infixed object 'him' after a (pwy a'e lladei 'who killed him'; a'e guelei 'who saw him') and 'her' with spirant mutation (a'e chladu yno 'and burying her there'); and the y of y gan 'from' (E gan Uanawydan 'from Manawydan') · also in e hun (ehun) 'self, own', unchanged for any person (eu kedymdeithon e hun 'their own companions'; synnyaw e hun 'watching for himself')
meuyl: meuyl (mefl) — shame, disgrace; noun m., used in the oath meuyl im 'shame on me' · also meuyl ar 'shame on' (Meuyl ar uy maryf i 'shame on my beard')
ymi: y (i) + mi — conjugated preposition 'to me' (pa gyuarwyd a uyd ymi)
ef: ef (ef) — 'he, him'; independent 3 sg. m. pronoun
i: i — (1) emphatic independent pronoun 'I/me', echoing a verb or conjugated preposition (rof i, arnaf i); (2) spelling of y 'to' before a vowel or l/w (i waret); (3) spelling of y 'his' before some words (i wisc hela 'his hunting-dress') · (4) after ohonawch, probably the 2 pl. echoing pronoun chwi with its ch run into the ending (ohonawch i 'of you')
wy: wynt (hwynt) — they; 3 pl. pronoun, spelling variant (heb wy 'said they') · also emphatic 'them' after a conjugated preposition (ganthunt wy 'from them', ohonunt wy 'of them')
onys: ony (oni) + 's 'it' — unless, if not (onys gwyr 'unless she knows it'); ony with infixed object pronoun s
ie: ie — yes; particle of assent, taking up what was just said
nit: nyt (nid) — negative particle 'not, there is not', spelling before a vowel (Nit oes; Nit yttoydwn)
oes: bot (bod) — to be; present 3 sg. existential 'there is' (Nit oes yndi nep)
achaws: achaws (achos) — cause, reason; noun m. ('Pa achaws' 'what reason, why')
uot: bot (bod) — to be; verbal noun, soft-mutated after a (ef a eill uot yn ediuar gennyf) · also soft as the complement of a verb (a dylyei uot 'that ought to be') · also soft-mutated after y 'his' (y uot yn colli 'that he was losing', lit. 'his being losing')
gwna: gwneuthur (gwneud) — to do, make; 2 sg. imperative 'make!, do!' (gwna oed a mi 'make an appointment with me')
ditheu: ditheu (dithau) — conjunctive form of ti 'you' (sg.), 'you for your part'
dy: dy — 'your' (sg.); possessive pronoun, causes soft mutation (dy gerennyd 'your friendship') · also written for the affixed pronoun di 'you' after the presentative wely (Ac wely dy yna dy uab 'and there, behold, is your son')
ewyllus: ewyllus (ewyllys) — will, desire, pleasure; noun m. (yn y ewyllus 'in his will')
gwypwn: gwybot (gwybod) — to know; 1 sg. imperfect subjunctive 'I would know' (pei ys gwypwn 'if I had known it'); no mutation
byt: byt (byd) — world; noun m. (o helgwn y byt 'of the hunting dogs of the world')
titheu: ti (ti) — you, for your part; conjunctive 2 sg. pronoun
bot: bot (bod) — to be; verbal noun (hyt na bo... uot 'so that there be...') · also introducing a reported fact, 'that (it) was' (adnabot bot eu hennill yn pallu 'knowing that their gain was failing'; clybot bot y gwyr 'hearing that the men were')
uydwn: bot (bod) — to be; 1 pl. future 'we will be', soft-mutated (b > u) after the relative a (Ni a uydwn drostaw 'we will stand for him')
gynghor: kynghor (cyngor) — counsel, advice, will; noun m., soft-mutated after possessive y 'his' (wrth y gynghor ef 'by his counsel'; gan gynghor 'by the counsel of') · also soft as the object of a verb (mi a wnn gynghor da 'I know good counsel') · also soft after a preceding adjective (yn y kyuyng gynghor 'in the narrow counsel') and as object (ni a gymerwn gynghor 'we will take counsel') · also soft after wrth (Reit oed im wrth gynghor 'I could do with counsel') and after pa (a pha gynghor 'and what counsel')
am: am — preposition 'about, around; concerning' (am y uynwgyl 'about his neck'; am dir a dayar 'about land') · also 'for, in return for' (am y gam 'for his wrong'; am pob un 'for each one')
gwnn: gwybot (gwybod) — to know; 1 sg. present 'I know', g often dropped after ny (ny wnn i 'I do not know')
arglwydes: arglwydes (arglwyddes) — lady; feminine of arglwyd, term of address
medwl: medwl (meddwl) — mind, thought; noun m. (yn y uryt ac yn y uedwl)
genhyf: gan (gan) — with, conjugated 1 sg. 'with me' (eres genhyf 'strange with me'; ryued oed genhyf 'it was a wonder with me'); the gan 'with' of opinion; no mutation
diuetha: diuetha (difetha) — to destroy; verbal noun (arnei e hun diuetha y mab 'against her that she herself destroyed the boy'; a'e diuetha 'and destroying him'); no mutation
llawen: llawen (llawen) — glad, gladly; adjective, base form (yn llawen)
kyrchwys: kyrchu (cyrchu) — to make for, charge at; 3 sg. preterite 'made for' in -wys (y kyrchwys y bleit 'he charged the wall'); no mutation after the particle y
orssed: gorssed (gorsedd) — mound; noun f., g lost by soft mutation after the article, as a feminine noun (yr orssed 'the mound', y'r orssed 'to the mound')
arberth: Arberth (Arberth) — proper name, Pwyll's chief court, modern Narberth in Dyfed
gantaw: gan (gan) — 'with him'; conjugated preposition, 3 sg. m., spelt gantaw (hyspys oed gantaw 'it was known to him'); no mutation
dwy: dwy (dwy) — two (f.); numeral, causes soft mutation of a following feminine noun (y dwy dyrnas 'the two kingdoms')
lle: lle (lle) — place; noun m., base unmutated form
byd: bot (bod) — to be; used two ways: 3 sg. future 'will be' (uyd elsewhere) and, with y-, the vivid present ual y byd 'as he is' · also 2 sg. imperative 'be!' (byd ditheu a'r got honn genhyt 'you be there with this bag') · also byt 'world', spelt with d (eliwlu y byd o lygot 'the world's host of mice'; the Red Book y byt)
yuelly: yuelly (felly) — thus, so, in that way; adverb, the particle y fused with uelly (a chyt kerych di uot yuelly 'though you wish it to be so'; Ac yuelly y gwnaethpwyt 'and so it was done'); no mutation
guelei: gwelet (gweld) — to see; 3 sg. imperfect, soft-mutated after y (Llyma y guelei ef 'there he saw')
attaw: at — conjugated preposition 'to him' (y marchawc a doeth attaw 'the horseman came to him')
hen: hen (hen) — old; adjective, as an epithet after a name (Heueyd Hen 'Hefeydd the Old')
amdanaw: am — conjugated preposition 'about him' (3 sg. m.); clothing/objects are 'about' a person (gwisc ... amdanaw)
neut: neut — affirmative particle, 'it is the case that' (neut teruynedic angheu y mi 'my death is determined') · neut is the affirmative particle neu in the form it takes before a vowel (as yd beside y), not neu + an infixed pronoun (neut athoed hi heibaw 'lo, she had gone past')
mlyned: blwydyn (blwyddyn) — year; plural blyned (modern blynedd), spelt mlyned (hyt ym penn y seith mlyned 'until the end of the seven years'); nasal-mutated (b>m) after seith 'seven' · also nasal-mutated after ugeint 'twenty' in pedwarugeint 'eighty' (pedwarugeint mlyned 'eighty years')
kyn: kyn (cyn) — before; with a verbal noun (kyn uy rodi 'before my being given') · also the equative particle 'as', softening the adjective (kyn debycket a'r mab 'as like as the boy') · also 'although', with the subjunctive (Kyn ny bwyf arglwydes 'though I am not a lady')
no: no (na) — than, comparative particle (no gyrru 'than driving'; no chyuedach)
pan: pan (pan) — when; temporal conjunction with a past-time clause (pan doeth) · also interrogative 'from where, whence' (pan doy di? 'where do you come from?')
welsei: gwelet (gweld) — to see; 3 sg. pluperfect 'had seen', soft-mutated after o'r a (o'r a welsei ef) · also soft after the negatives na and ny (hyt na welsei dyn 'so that no man had seen'; ny welsei dyn)
na: na — (1) negative particle in a subordinate clause, 'not' (na dywedy di); (2) 'neither/nor' in a series (na guas ystauell, na swydawc) · also negative imperative 'do not', with soft mutation (na ouyn di 'do not ask'; na yrrwch geu arnaf 'do not lay a lie on me'; na hawl ef 'do not claim him')
dyn: dyn (dyn) — man, person; noun m. (y dyn eithaf 'the farthest man')
mil: mil (mil) — animal, beast, living creature; noun m. (na mil 'nor any beast'); radical after na 'nor'; not the numeral 'thousand'
eithyr: eithyr (eithr) — except; conjunction/preposition (eithyr gadu 'except to leave')
gyt: kyt (cyd) — together; in y gyt (a) 'together (with)' (y gyt ac wynt 'together with them')
yny: yny (hyd oni) — until; so that; conjunction, with a vivid present (yny hyllt, yny dyrr, yny uyd) or the subjunctive for a future goal (yny delych) · also in Ac ar yny llyma, a slip for ar hynny 'thereupon', kept as written (the Red Book has ar hynny) (Ac ar yny, llyma y teulu 'and thereupon, behold the warband')
golles: colli (colli) — to lose; here without an object, 'be lost'; 3 sg. preterite (neur golles y mab 'the boy has been lost'); soft-mutated (c>g) after neur (neu + the perfective ry)
deu: deu (dau) — two (m.); numeral, causes soft mutation of a following noun (y deu wrenhin 'the two kings')
dyd: dyd (dydd) — day; noun m. (y dyd 'the day'; dyd da 'good day')
da: da — good; adjective, also 'goods, wealth' as a noun (treulaw dy da 'spending your wealth')
it: itt (iti) — to you; 2 sg. conjugated preposition, spelling variant with single t (achos it heuyt)
rodo: rodi (rhoi) — to give; 3 sg. present subjunctive 'may he give' (Duw a rodo da ywch 'may God give you good'); after the particle a soft mutation of rh is not distinguishable in the spelling (r for rh)
grayssaw: graessaw (croeso) — welcome; noun m. (a grayssaw wrthywch 'and welcome to you'); the g- is the word's own initial in this spelling (not a mutation here)
wrthyt: wrth (wrth) + ti — conjugated preposition 'to/at you' (Dywedaf wrthyt; chadw kywirdeb wrthyt titheu)
doy: dyuot (dod) — to come; 2 sg. present 'you come' (pan doy di 'where do you come from?') · also 3 sg. imperfect 'would come', a variant of doey (ny doy gof udunt wy dim 'no memory of anything came to them')
di: di — 'you' (sg.), echoing pronoun after a verb or possessive (y pryny di; dy gerennyd di); also the object 'you' (ni ladaf i di)
o: o (o) — (1) 'of, from' preposition; (2) 'if' before a verb (o gwneuthum gam 'if I did wrong') · also 'on, by' (o pedestric 'on foot'), 'out of, from' (o'th garyat ti 'from love of you'), 'of' a kind (pryt … o uorwyn 'the looks of (any) maiden') · also agent after a verbal noun, 'by' (troi o Pwyll y got 'Pwyll turning the bag'); o gosp 'of punishment'
loygyr: Proper name — Lloegr, England (spelt Loygyr); softened (ll>l) as the object straight after the verb (Kyrchwn Loygyr 'let us make for England')
weleis: gwelet (gweld) — to see; 1 sg. preterite 'I saw/have seen', soft-mutated after ny (Ny weleis ansyberwyt uwy)
onyt: onyt (onid) — unless; conjunction (onyt ti a'm gwrthyt 'unless (it be) you (who) reject me')
pedwar: pedwar (pedwar) — four; numeral m.; no mutation (yn pedwar dryll 'into four pieces'; a predicative yn would soften it, not shown)
thitheu: titheu (tithau) — you for your part; 2 sg. conjunctive pronoun, spirant-mutated after a 'and' (A thitheu 'and you')
awr: awr (awr) — hour; noun f. (hyt yr awr hon 'until this hour'); no mutation (vowel)
honn: hon (hon) — 'this' (f.); variant spelling of hon (no'r ulwydyn honn 'than this year')
mynet: mynet (mynd) — to go; verbal noun (amser mynet y uwyta 'time to go to eat')
drwy: trwy (trwy) — through; preposition, soft-mutated form (drwy y dewred ef 'through his valour')
wlat: gwlat (gwlad) — land, country; noun f., soft-mutated after the feminine article or possessive (y wlat; i'th wlat) · also soft as the object of a verb, with an adverb between (ny welsynt eiryoet wlat gyuanhedach 'they had never seen a more settled land')
wyf: bot (bod) — to be; 1 sg. present 'I am' (Brenhin corunawc wyf i)
parth: parth (parth) — towards, side, direction; noun m./preposition (parth a'y lys 'towards his court')
m: 'm — infixed/proclitic pronoun, apostrophe half of a'm, y'm, o'm etc.: 'my' (possessive, triggers soft mutation) or 'me' (object) · with h- before a following vowel (o'm hanwod 'against my will'); as 'my' before a verbal noun it may stand for that noun's object (a'm rodi 'and my giving' = and giving me); as 'me' after a relative (a'm gwrthyt 'who rejects me')
gwlat: gwlat (gwlad) — land, country; noun f. (ar gynghor uy gwlat 'to the counsel of my country'); no mutation shown after uy 'my' (the nasal mutation, ngwlat, is not written)
uy: uy (fy) — my; possessive pronoun, triggers nasal mutation (uy anryded; uy nghyffes; uy gherennyd)
hun: hun (hun) — self, own; also 'sleep' as a separate noun by context (e hunan/e hun 'himself'; kymryt hun 'to take sleep')
pha: pa (pa) — what, which; interrogative, spirant-mutated after a 'and' (a pha wlat 'and what land')
weith: gwaith (gwaith) — work, make, pattern, manner; noun m. (MW gweith); g lost by soft mutation after ar (ar weith taryaneu da 'after the pattern of good shields, on the work of good shields'); the sense 'manner, pattern' is a little uncertain · also soft-mutated (gw>w) as the object of welsynt (y lle ny welsynt eiryoet weith 'where they had never seen work'); gweith 'time' is possible but less likely
yndaw: yn (yn) + ef — conjugated preposition 'in him' (angheuawl dyrnawt yndaw ynteu; yssyd yndaw ef)
welaf: gwelet (gweld) — to see; 1 sg. present 'I see', soft-mutated after a (mi a welaf 'I see')
law: llaw (llaw) — hand; noun f., soft-mutated after heb in heb law 'past, beside' (heb law yr orssed 'past the mound') · also 'side' in ar neill law 'on one side' (ar neill law Pwyll 'on one side of Pwyll'), soft after neill; 'hand' after possessive 'th (y'th law 'in your hand') · also soft after y 'his' (dodi y law 'putting his hand')
drwc: drwc (drwg) — evil, harm, wrong; noun m. (ny chewch un drwc 'you will get no harm'); no mutation · also the adjective 'bad', as a fronted predicate (ys drwc a gedymdeith uuosti 'a bad companion you were')
gueda: gweddu (gweddu) — to suit, befit; 3 sg. present 'suits' (goreu y gueda arnaw Pryderi 'Pryderi suits him best'), spelt gueda; no mutation after the particle y
wr: gwr (gŵr) — man; noun m., soft-mutated as object (ansyberwyt uwy ar wr) · also soft after y 'to' (y wr 'to a man, to a husband') · also soft in address (A wr 'O man') and after ryw 'kind of' (pa ryw wr 'what kind of man') · also subject directly after a negated verb, soft-mutated (Ny doey wr mawr 'no great man would come')
kyfryw: kyfryw (cyfryw) — such, similar; adjective (yn y kyfryw le a hwnn 'in such a place as this')
rof: rwng (rhwng) + i — conjugated preposition 'between me' (y rof i a Duw 'between me and God')
keueis: caffael (cael) — to get, have; 1 sg. preterite 'I got' (y keueis wynt 'I had them'); no mutation after the particle y
wnaf: gwneuthur (gwneud) — to do, make; 1 sg. present/future 'I will do', soft-mutated after a (mi a wnaf hynny) · also 'I will see to it, bring it about that' (mi a wnaf na chaffo ef uiui uyth 'I will see that he never gets me'); auxiliary (Y gymryt a wnaf 'I will take it')
rac: rac (rhag) — before, lest, to prevent, for fear of; preposition (dyro ui idaw rac anglot yt 'give me to him to spare you dishonour') · also 'from' after verbs of saving (waret rac hynn 'to deliver from this')
gueith: gweith (gwaith) — work, labour, craft, the thing made; noun m., gu- spells gw- (o'r gueith hwnnw 'of that work'; y gueith wynteu 'their work'); radical after the article and after y standing for eu 'their'
rodaf: rodi (rhoi) — to give, put; 1 sg. present/future 'I will give/put' (mi a'th rodaf di)
nac: nac — (1) negative used in a direct answer, repeating the verb, 'no' (Nac attygaf 'I will not'); (2) 'nor' before a vowel (nac ymdidan) · also negative imperative 'do not' (nac arch dim 'do not ask anything') · also Nac ef 'no', literally 'not it', refusing a proposal (Nac ef, heb y Manawydan 'No, said Manawydan')
nys: ny + 's — negative particle ny with infixed 3 sg. object pronoun 's 'it': 'not it' (nys attygy 'you will not withdraw it') · also 'him, her' (nys mynnaf 'I do not want him')
ony: ony (oni) — unless, until; conjunction ('no, unless …'), causes spirant mutation of c, p, t (ony chyuyt 'unless there rise') · also with soft mutation of g (ony wybydaf i 'if I do not find out')
ny: ny (ni/nid) — negative particle 'not', base form before a consonant with soft mutation · also spirant mutation of c, p, t (ny chewch 'you will not get'; ny thygyawd 'it did not avail'); soft mutation of g (ny wybydei 'knew not')
aeth: mynet (mynd) — to go; 3 sg. preterite 'went' (a'y vreic a aeth attaw 'and his wife went to him')
val: ual (fel) — as; conjunction, spelt val (Ac val y bydynt 'and as they were')
nachaf: nachaf (no modern form) — behold, lo; presentative particle that sets the scene before the eyes (nachaf un o'r llongeu 'behold one of the ships'); no mutation
ataw: at (at) + ef — 'to him'; conjugated preposition, 3 sg. m. (a aeth ataw ef 'went to him'); no mutation
uarch: march (march) — horse; noun m., soft-mutated after ar (y ar uarch erchlas mawr 'on a big dapple-grey horse') · also soft-mutated after y 'his' (y uarch 'his horse')
ro: rodi (rhoi) — to give; 3 sg. present subjunctive 'may he give', in a wish after the particle a; r- shows no mutation (Duw a ro da yt 'may God give you good')
manawydan: Proper name — Manawydan, son of Llŷr, brother of Bendigeidfran; radical (subject, after a 'and')
wneuthur: gwneuthur (gwneud) — to do, make; verbal noun (y wneuthur kynnadeu at Pwyll 'to send envoys to Pwyll', literally 'to make messengers'); soft-mutated (gw>w) after the preposition y 'to'
ansawd: ansawd — (1) form, appearance (pryt ac ansawd 'form and appearance'); (2) means, condition (Nit oes ansawd y mi 'I have no means')
wnaeth: gwneuthur (gwneud) — to do, make; 3 sg. preterite 'he did', soft-mutated after a; auxiliary in 'verbal noun + a wnaeth' (dechreu ymdidan a wnaeth)
dihenyd: dihenyd (dihenydd) — end, death, especially the death a man deserves; noun m. (nyt oed dihenyd arnaf uy llad y mywn got 'it was no fit death for me, to be killed in a bag')
arnaw: ar — conjugated preposition 'on him, on it' (llithiau dy erchwys dy hun arnaw 'feeding your own pack on it')
welet: gwelet (gweld) — to see; verbal noun, soft-mutated after dy 'your' (dy welet ti 'seeing you', literally 'your seeing') · also soft after o 'from, because of' (o welet gwr kymeint a gerynt 'from seeing a man so loved by them') · also soft after am 'for, because of' (am welet y cledyf 'for seeing the sword') · also soft-mutated (gw>w) as a verbal noun directly after the verb (ryuedu a wnaethant welet y gaer 'they marvelled to see the fort')
dygaf: dwyn (dwyn) — to bring, carry; 1 sg. present 'I bring' (y dygaf uy nghyffes 'I bring my confession')
nas: ny + 's — negative particle ny with infixed 3 sg. object pronoun 's 'it/him': 'that not it/him' (ual nas dylyei)
gwnaf: gwneuthur (gwneud) — to do, make; 1 sg. present/future 'I will do' (mi a wnaf hynny 'I will do that')
guir: gwir (gwir) — truth, true; noun m., fronted object (guir a dyweit 'he speaks truth')
guerth: guerth (gwerth) — worth, value; noun m. (guerth can carw 'the worth of a hundred stags')
dim: dim — anything, nothing; indefinite pronoun (ny russya dim ragot 'nothing will obstruct before you')
deir: tri (tri) — three; feminine form teir (tair), written deir; soft-mutated (t>d) after 'e 'his' (a'e deir grofd 'and his three crofts')
uynhaf: mynnu (mynnu) — to want, wish; 1 sg. present 'I want' (na uynhaf 'I do not want'); soft-mutated (m>u, = f) after the negative na · also soft-mutated (m>u, = f) after the affirmative particle a (mi a uynhaf 'I will want, I mean to')
dyly: dylyu (dylu) — to owe, be bound to; 3 sg. present 'owes it' (pawb a'y dyly 'everyone owes it')
en: yn (yn) — in; preposition, spelt en (En Iwerdon 'in Ireland'); no mutation (vowel)
uympwy: mympwy (mympwy) — whim, wish, fancy; noun m., soft-mutated (m>u) after possessive y 'his' (a'y uympwy 'and his fancy')
sef: sef (sef) — it is (this), that is; presentative particle introducing an explanation or answer
llinin: llinyn (llinyn) — string, cord, thread; noun m., spelt llinin (ac a llinin 'and with a string'); radical after a 'with'
uynwgyl: mynwgyl (mynwgl) — neck; noun m., soft-mutated after am (am y uynwgyl 'about his neck')
dyrchauael: dyrchafael (dyrchafu) — to raise, lift up; verbal noun (dyrchauael taryan 'raising a shield'; yn dyrchauael 'rising, prospering'); no mutation
welei: gwelet (gweld) — to see; 3 sg. imperfect 'he saw' (welei), soft-mutated after a (ef a welei lannerch) · also 'would see' (neu ynteu a welei rywedawt 'or else he would see a wonder')
yniuer: niuer (nifer) — company, host; noun m. with prosthetic y- (yr yniuer y buam doe 'the company that we were yesterday')
kyrchu: kyrchu (cyrchu) — to make for, head towards; verbal noun (Kyrchu y llys a oruc ynteu)
wyt: bot (bod) — to be; 2 sg. present 'you are' (pwy wyt ti 'who are you')
ty: ty (tŷ) — house; noun m. (yn y ty yd oed cassec 'in the house was a mare'); no mutation
ponyt: ponyt (ponid) — 'is it not?', negative question particle, pony with t before a vowel (Ponyt oed da iti 'would it not be well for you'); no mutation
uu: bot (bod) — to be; 3 sg. preterite 'was' (bu), soft-mutated after a (tirionwch... a uu y ryngthunt) · also soft-mutated after tra 'while' (tra uu da ganthunt 'while it was good with them') · also soft-mutated after yny 'until' (yny uu damunet gantunt 'until there was desire in them') and as after the relative a left unwritten (A hwnnw uu y trydyd dyn 'and that one was the third man')
can: can — hundred; numeral, also 'white' (Hafgan = haf + can 'summer-white'); here in guerth can carw 'the worth of a hundred stags'
genhyt: gan — conjugated preposition 'with you' (2 sg.), a variant spelling of gennyt (a'r got honn genhyt 'and this bag with you')
yrdaw: yr (er) + ef — 'for him, for his sake'; conjugated preposition, 3 sg. m. (a wnaethom yrdaw ef 'what we did for him'); no mutation
thi: ti (ti) — you; 2 sg. pronoun, spirant-mutated after a 'and, with' (gyt a thi 'together with you')
mor: mor (mor) — so, how; adverbial intensifier, triggers soft mutation (mor lwydannus) · also môr 'sea' (hyt y mor 'as far as the sea'); noun m., no mutation
kanys: kanys (canys) — because, for, since; conjunction (Kanys y noss y keueist y mab 'for the night you got the boy'); no mutation
aryant: aryant (arian) — silver, money; noun m. (llathen aryant 'a rod of silver'); no mutation (vowel)
arall: arall — other, another; adjective (yr erchwys arall 'the other pack') · also pronoun 'another (woman)' (heb arall 'said another')
canys: canys — since, for, because; conjunction (canys dechreueist uy llad 'since you have begun to kill me')
wely: gwelet (gweld) — to see; 2 sg. present 'you will see', soft-mutated after a (ti a wely a wneuthum i yrot ti) · also in the presentative (a) wely di 'do you see?' = 'behold' (Ac wely dy yna dy uab 'and there, behold, is your son'; the Red Book has weldy), softened after the question particle a, which is absorbed
maes: maes (maes) — field, open ground; noun m. (o'r maes hwnn 'of this field', of those here)
meirch: march (march) — horse; noun pl. (meirch a milgwn 'horses and greyhounds')
maent: bot (bod) — to be; 3 pl. present 'they are' (y maent yn lluossauc 'they are numerous'); no mutation
arnunt: ar — conjugated preposition 'on them' (Sef lliw oed arnunt 'this was the colour that was on them')
cany: cany — 'since … not'; conjunction can 'since' + the negative ny, softening the verb (Cany welas ef 'since he did not see')
mynny: mynnu (mynnu) — to want, wish; 2 sg. present 'you wish' (y mynny di 'that you wish')
riannon: Riannon (Rhiannon) — proper name, daughter of Heueyd Hen
gehy: caffael (cael) — to get; 2 sg. present/future 'you will get' (ti a gehy ychwanegu 'you will get an increase'); soft-mutated (c>g) after the particle a
guaret: guaret (gwared) — to deliver, remove, rid; verbal noun (yr guaret gormes hwnnw 'to remove that oppression')
hut: hut (hud) — magic, illusion, enchantment; noun m. (ystyr hut 'a meaning of magic')
cantref: cantref (cantref) — a 'hundred townships', the main administrative division of medieval Wales; noun m. (seith cantref Dyuet 'the seven cantrefs of Dyfed')
dyuet: Dyuet (Dyfed) — proper name, the region of south-west Wales
heuyt: heuyt (hefyd) — also, either; adverb (Ni wydwn achos it heuyt 'I did not know a reason for you either')
gwybot: gwybot (gwybod) — to know; verbal noun (ef yn gwybot y uot yn uab 'he knowing that he was a son'); no mutation
pwy: pwy (pwy) — who; interrogative pronoun (pwy wyt ti 'who are you')
gwreic: gwreic (gwraig) — wife, woman; noun f., meaning as context decides (a'y wreic 'and his wife')
doeth: dyuot (dod) — to come; 3 sg. preterite 'came' (a doeth 'and came')
miui: mi (mi) — I/me; emphatic 1 sg. pronoun, fuller spelling of mi (A miui a af)
uab: mab (mab) — son; noun m., soft-mutated after a personal name in a patronymic (Guawl uab Clut 'Gwawl son of Clud') · also soft after predicative yn (yn uab y wr arall 'a son of another man'; yn uab y Pwyll 'a son of Pwyll') · also soft in apposition to a noun (uy nei, uab uy chwaer 'my nephew, son of my sister') and in address (Oy a uab Duw 'O son of God')
coet: coet (coed) — wood, forest; noun m. (dan y coet 'under the wood')
dodeis: dodi (dodi) — to put, place; 1 sg. preterite 'I put' (-eis) (E dodeis inheu ar gynghor uy gwlat 'I put it to the counsel of my country'); no mutation after the particle E
dial: dial (dial) — vengeance, revenge; noun m. (na dial uyth 'nor vengeance ever') · also verbal noun 'to avenge' after y 'to' (y dial Paluawt Branwen 'to avenge the Blow of Branwen'), softened, d spelling dd so the change does not show
guawl: Gwawl — proper name (Gwawl uab Clut), also gwawl 'light, radiance' as a common word; spelt guawl, no mutation as the subject (Guawl uab Clut)
clut: Clud (Clud) — proper name, the father of Gwawl (Gwawl uab Clut); the name is spelt Clut
gedymdeithas: kedymdeithas (cydymdeithas) — fellowship, companionship; noun f., soft-mutated after y (kedymdeithas y ryngthunt 'fellowship between them')
pryderi: Pryderi (Pryderi) — proper name, the son of Pwyll and Rhiannon, named from pryder 'care'; no mutation
guare: gware (chwarae) — to play, play with; verbal noun, spelt guare (guare a'r got 'to play with the bag'; guare broch yg got 'the game of badger in the bag') · also noun 'game, sport, trick' (y tremic hwnnw a'r guare 'that insult and the sport')
broch: broch (broch) — badger; noun m. (Broch 'badger', the cry in the game; guare broch yg got 'badger-in-the-bag')
gwnaeth: gwneuthur (gwneud) — to do, make; 3 sg. preterite 'he did', unmutated after the particle y (Kyntaf y gwnaeth ef ymdidan)
pwyll: Pwyll — proper name, the tale's protagonist; means 'sense, discretion' (pwyll)
penn: penn (pen) — head, end; noun m., base form (Penn Annwuyn 'Head of Annwfn')
annwn: Annwn — Annwfn, the realm of Arawn; proper name, in Penn Annwn 'Head of Annwfn' (Pwyll ynteu Penn Annwn); spelt Annwn here, Annwuyn in the first part (and in the Red Book here)
llys: llys (llys) — court; noun f., base form
eueyd: Heueyd (Hefeydd) — proper name, Rhiannon's father; spelt Eueyd without the h- (Eueyd Hen 'Heueyd the Old') · also Eueyd Hir, Efeydd Hir, a messenger of Bendigeidfran in the Second Branch (Kyuodwch, Uanawydan uab Llyr, ac Eueyd Hir 'rise, Manawydan, and Efeydd Hir'); radical
guedy: guedy (gwedi) — after; preposition (A guedy y medwl hwnnw 'and after that thought')
uyn: mynnu (mynnu) — to wish, want; 3 sg. present 'wants' (A uyn ef dyuot y'r tir 'does he want to come ashore?'); soft-mutated (m>u) after the interrogative particle a · also uy (fy) 'my', with the nasal mutation of d- written as n on the possessive (uyn diua i 'my destruction')
teulu: teulu (teulu) — household-troop, warband, a lord's retinue; noun m. (later came to mean 'family')
erchi: erchi (erchi) — to ask, request, bid; verbal noun (y erchi it 'to ask of you')
diua: diua (difa) — to destroy; verbal noun, here 'destroying, destruction' (uyn diua i 'my destroying'); the nasal mutation of d- after uy 'my' is written as n on the possessive (uyn), the noun itself keeping d (= fy nifa)
nos: nos (nos) — night; noun f. (y nos honno 'that night')
gyntaf: kyntaf (cyntaf) — first; superlative, soft-mutated after y (ar y gossot kyntaf 'at the first onset') · also adverbial 'fastest, soonest' (ual y gallei gyntaf 'as fast as he could')
hunein: hun (hun) — self; plural hunein (modern hunain) in ny hunein 'ourselves' (arnam ny hunein 'on ourselves'); pronoun/noun; no mutation
eil: eil (ail) — second; ordinal numeral (yr eil 'the second')
tryded: trydyd (trydydd) — third; ordinal, feminine form tryded (trydedd) (A honno oed tryded prif rieni 'and she was the third chief ...'); no mutation (soft mutation after predicative yn is not written: yn tryded)
gwraged: gwreic (gwraig) — woman, wife; noun f., plural gwraged (modern gwragedd) (a gwraged 'and women'; gwyr a gwraged 'men and women')
im: im (i mi) — to me; conjugated preposition, contracted spelling (Meuyl im 'shame to me')
beichawc: beichiawc (beichiog) — pregnant; adjective after its plural noun (pump gwraged beichawc 'five pregnant women'); radical
ueichawc: beichawc (beichiog) — pregnant, burdened; adjective (uy mot y ueichawc 'that I was pregnant'); soft-mutated (b>u) after the predicative particle y (yn)
bu: bot (bod) — to be; 3 sg. preterite 'was' (a uu 'was'; Llawen uu 'glad was')
dala: dala (dal) — to hold, seize, take on; verbal noun (dechreuis gwyr y wlat dala trymuryt 'the men of the land began to take sorrow'); no mutation
minheu: minheu (minnau) — I for my part; conjunctive 1 sg. pronoun, beside innheu (Minheu a baraf 'and I for my part will cause')
yti: y (i) + ti — conjugated preposition 'to you', variant spelling (pa furyf y caf i dy gerennyd di... yti)
uynny: mynnu (mynnu) — to want, wish; 2 sg. present 'you want', soft-mutated after a (a uynny 'that you want')
llyna: llyna (dyna) — there is, behold that; presentative particle, distal counterpart of llyma
bo: bot (bod) — to be; 3 sg. present subjunctive 'may be' (Vrth ual y bo dy anryded 'according as your rank may be')
uyth: byth (byth) — ever; with a negative, 'never'; adverb, soft-mutated (b>u) when used adverbially after the verb (dywedy di uyth 'you ever say'; na chaffo ef uiui uyth 'that he may never get me'; a uyd llawn dy got uyth 'will your bag ever be full')
dotter: dodi (dodi) — to put; impersonal present subjunctive 'is put' (yr a dotter yndi uyth 'however much is put into it')
hynn: hynn (hyn) — 'this'; demonstrative, substantive use in ual hynn 'like this, thus' · also adjective 'this' after its noun (seith cantref hynn 'these seven cantrefs')
dioer: dioer — assuredly, indeed; an oath, a worn-down Duw a wyr 'God knows'
benn: penn (pen) — head, top, end; noun m.; soft-mutated (p>b) after ar 'on' (ar benn gossed 'on top of a mound'; ar benn y pethewnos 'at the end of the fortnight') · also soft after y 'his' (gauas y benn 'found his head') and after am 'about' (am benn hwnnw 'about that one's head') · also soft after a preceding adjective (Yspydawt Urdaul Benn 'the Hospitality of the Honoured Head') and after the feminine noun yspydawt (Yspydaut Benn 'the Hospitality of the Head') · also soft-mutated (p>b) after uch 'above' (uch benn llech 'above a slab')
cwbyl: cwbl (cwbl) — whole, complete; adjective/noun m., spelt cwbyl (kynn dyuot cwbyl o'r oet 'before the whole of the term came'); no mutation
gouut: gouut (gofid) — grief, sorrow, trouble; noun m. (y gouut a oed arnat 'the grief that was on you'); no mutation after the article
weithon: weithon (weithian) — now, at last; adverb, always in this softened form (gweith 'time' + hon 'this'); par weithon wahard 'have (them) forbidden now'
ryd: rhydd (rhydd) — free; adjective (yny uo ryd y wyr 'until his men are free')
wynteu: wynt (hwynt) — they, for their part; conjunctive 3 pl. pronoun (Wynteu hagen ni wybuyssynt)
kyuodi: kyuodi (cyfodi) — to rise, get up; verbal noun (kyuodi a oruc 'he rose')
herbyn: erbyn (erbyn) — meeting; in yn y herbyn 'to meet her', with h- before the vowel after y 'her'
eisted: eisted (eistedd) — to sit; verbal noun (eisted a wnaethant 'they sat')
neu: neu (neu) — (1) 'or' (kymriw neu archolleu 'injury or wounds'; neu ynteu 'or else'); (2) the affirmative particle neu 'lo, indeed' before a verb, neut before a vowel, neur with infixed 'r (see neut, neir)
ry: ry — perfective verbal particle 'has, had' before a verb; causes soft mutation (ry adoed 'had gone')
geueist: caffael (cael) — to get; 2 sg. preterite 'you got' (gauael gadarn a geueist 'a firm hold you got')
gwbyl: cwbyl (cwbl) — whole, complete; adjective; soft-mutated (c>g) as the predicate after uu (yny uu gwbyl idaw y dal 'until his payment was complete to him')
neb: neb (neb) — anyone; pronoun, used with a positive sense in relative/superlative clauses (o'r a welsei neb 'that anyone had seen') · also 'anyone' under a negative = 'no one' (ny thykya y neb ymlit 'it avails no one to pursue') · also in y neb a 'the one who/to whom' (y neb a dylyer y kymryt y ganthaw 'the one from whom one ought to take it')
edrych: edrych (edrych) — to look; verbal noun (edrych ar y carw 'to look at the stag')
gylch: kylch (cylch) — circle, circuit, surrounding; noun m. (yn y gylch 'about him'); soft-mutated (k>g) after the possessive y 'his'
holl: holl (holl) — all, whole; adjective, precedes its noun causing soft mutation (yr holl gyuoeth 'the whole realm')
kyuanhed: cyfanhedd (cyfanhedd) — dwelling, habitation, inhabited place; noun m. (y kyuanhed 'the dwellings'; ay ty ay kyuanhed 'either house or dwelling'); radical after the article y; cf. the adjective gyuanhedach
buant: bot (bod) — to be; 3 pl. preterite 'they were' (Ny buant 'they were not')
oreu: goreu (gorau) — best; superlative of da 'good', softened after a feminine noun (y neges oreu 'the best errand') · also soft as predicate after bu (yn gystal ac y bu oreu 'as good as he was best') · also soft-mutated (g lost) after yn (yn oreu yn y byt 'best in the world')
phan: pan (pan) — when; spirant-mutated after a 'and' (A phan doeth yno) · also spirant-mutated after no 'than' (no phan uuassei 'than when he had been')
uydei: bot (bod) — to be; 3 sg. habitual imperfect 'would be, used to be' (bydei), soft-mutated after a fronted word, the relative a being understood (pellaf uydei hitheu 'the farther she would be')
porth: porth (porth) — gate, gateway, entrance; noun m. (y porth 'the gate'); no mutation
wedy: gwedy (gwedi) — after; preposition, spelt without g, as in modern wedi (wedy bwyta 'after the eating'); the loss of g is a variant spelling, there is no clear softening word
hitheu: hitheu (hithau) — conjunctive form of hi 'she', 'she for her part'
carchar: carchar (carchar) — prison; noun m. (yn y carchar e hun 'in his own prison': after y 'his' one would expect y garchar, as the Red Book has; the White Book's reading is uncertain)
gelwit: galw (galw) — to call; 3 sg. impersonal imperfect 'he was called' (y gelwit Pwyll Penn Annwuyn)
teruyna: terfynu (terfynu) — to end, finish; 3 sg. present 'ends' (y teruyna y geing hon yma 'this branch ends here'); no mutation after the particle y
geing: keing (cainc) — branch, strand, a branch of the Mabinogi; noun f. (y geing hon 'this branch'); soft-mutated (k>g) after the feminine article y
